headlines.title: RTX Q3 Deep Dive: Defense Awards and Commercial Aftermarket Drive Upward Guidance
headlines.summary: Aerospace and defense company Raytheon (NYSE:RTX) reported revenue ahead of Wall Street’s expectations in Q3 2026, with sales up 11.1% year on year to $24.97 billion. The company’s full-year revenue guidance of $97.25 billion at the midpoint came in 1.1% above analysts’ estimates. Its non-GAAP profit of $2.26 per share was 27% above analysts’ consensus estimates.

headlines.title: RTX's Pratt & Whitney Canada introduces certified PT9 engine
headlines.summary: Pratt & Whitney Canada today unveiled its latest turboprop engine with a new centerline that delivers 33% more power at altitude and reduces fuel consumption by 20%, compared to previous generation engines. The engine, which amassed more than 14,000 development hours, was recently certified by Transport Canada. Pratt & Whitney is an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business.

headlines.title: RTX's Collins Aerospace launches Tower MicroELITE surveillance solution at San Bernardino International Airport
headlines.summary: Collins Aerospace, an RTX (NYSE: RTX) business, has announced the launch of its Tower MicroELITE (TME) surveillance solution, a secure, scalable digital display system that enhances air traffic controller situational awareness. San Bernardino Airport (SBD) became the first to deploy the new solution, providing the integrated surveillance data tracking needed to accommodate a rapid increase in airspace operations.

headlines.title: RTX (RTX) Q3 Earnings Put Margin Gains Ahead Of Stock Price Reaction
headlines.summary: RTX just cleared another psychological test. After releasing Q3 2026 earnings, the stock closed at US$193.34, only 0.6% higher on the day, even as the company reported adjusted sales of US$25.0b and adjusted earnings per share of US$2.26. The headline story is margin power. Adjusted segment operating profit reached US$3.9b with roughly 310 basis points of segment margin expansion, yet the share price barely budged.

headlines.title: RTX: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
headlines.summary: Margin expansion at Collins Aerospace shows RTX can grow sales while cutting costs, a rare combination that matters for long-term returns.

description: RTX Corporation, an aerospace and defense company, provides systems and services for commercial, military, and government customers worldwide. It operates through three segments: Collins Aerospace (Collins), Pratt & Whitney, and Raytheon. The Collins segment offers aerospace and defense products, and aftermarket services for civil and military aircraft manufacturers and commercial airlines, as well as regional, business, and general aviation, defense, and commercial space operations. This segment designs, manufactures, and supplies electric power generation and management and distribution, environmental control, flight control, air data and aircraft sensing, engine control, and engine nacelle systems, as well as engine components; cabin interiors, including seating, oxygen, food and beverage preparation, storage and galley, lavatory, and wastewater management systems; connected aviation solutions and services; and systems solutions for connected battlespace, test and training range systems, crew escape systems, and simulation and training. It also provides spare parts, overhaul and repair, engineering and technical support, training and fleet management solutions, and asset and information management services. The Pratt & Whitney segment supplies aircraft engines for commercial, military, business jet, and general aviation customers; and produces, sells, and services military and commercial auxiliary power units, as well as offers fleet management and aftermarket maintenance, repair, and overhaul services. The Raytheon segment provides defensive and offensive threat detection, tracking, and mitigation capabilities for government and commercial customers. This segment offers sensors, mission orchestration and satellite control products, and software. The company was formerly known as Raytheon Technologies Corporation and changed its name to RTX Corporation in July 2023. RTX Corporation was incorporated in 1934 and is headquartered in Arlington, Virginia.
